chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Ibn Muskān, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام.
Concerning a man who prayed two rakʿahs in a garment in which there was a spot of janābah, then came to know, he عليه السلام said: He must begin the salat (prayer) again.

He said: And I asked him about a man who prays while on his garment there is janābah or blood, until he finishes his salat (prayer), then comes to know. He عليه السلام said: His salat (prayer) has passed as valid, and there is nothing upon him.

key_terms.جَنَابَةٌ: major ritual impurity present on the garment
key_terms.دَمٌ: blood as a form of najasah
key_terms.نُكْتَةُ جَنَابَةٍ: a spot or trace of janābah on the garment
key_terms.يَبْتَدِئَ: to begin again, i.e. restart the salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone discovers janābah or blood on his garment after or during salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of praying in a garment affected by najasah discovered only afterward. If one learns of it during the salat (prayer), he must restart it; but if he only learns after completing the salat (prayer), then the prayer stands and nothing is required of him.
